docs.title: Git
docs.text: We use Commitizen to manage both an auto-generated Changelog and incrementing the release version following semver. For both of these automated outputs to work well, please follow the Conventional Commits style, which is described in more detail below.

docs.title: Commitizen Types and Scopes
docs.text:
type(scope): description

  • Types
    • fix: A bug fix
    • feat: A new feature
    • docs: Documentation-only changes (code comments, separate docs)
    • style: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, missing semi-colons)
    • perf: A code change that improves performance
    • refactor: A change to production code that is not a fix, feat, or perf
    • test: Adding missing or correcting existing tests
    • build: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
    • ci: Changes to our CI configuration files and scripts
    • A ! can be used to indicate a breaking change (refactor!: drop support for Node 6)
    • SemVer Rules
      • Based on commit type, the version will be auto-incremented: fix : PATCH // feat : MINOR // BREAKING CHANGE : MAJOR
  • Scopes
    • A Class, File name, Issue Number, other appropriate noun. As examples: build(uv): bump requests to v3 or style(#32): add missing type annotations
  • Tips
    • What if a commit fits multiple types?
      • Go back and make multiple commits whenever possible. Part of the benefit of Conventional Commits is the focus on more organized and intentional changes
    • Use git rebase -i to fix commit names prior to merging if incorrect types/scopes are used

docs.title: Git Description Guidelines
docs.text:
• Commit message guidelines
    • Full sentence with verb (lowercase) and concise description. Below are modified examples for Conventional Commits
      • fix(roles): bug in admin role permissions
      • feat(ui): implement new button design
      • build(pip): upgrade package to remove vulnerabilities
      • refactor: file structure to improve code readability
      • perf(cli): rewrite methods
      • feat(api): endpoints to implement new customer dashboard
  • How to write a good commit message
    • A diff will tell you what changed, but only the commit message can properly tell you why.
    • Keep in mind: This has all been said before.
    • From the seven rules of a great Git commit message:
      • (2) Try for 50 characters, but consider 72 the hard limit
      • (7) Use the body to explain what and why vs. how

docs.title: Issue Labels and Milestones
docs.text:
Personal Guide

  • For Issue Labels, see [labels.yml][labels]
  • Milestones
    • Current Tasks: main milestone (name could change based on a specific project, sprint, or month)
    • Next Tasks
    • Blue Sky
Research
  • [Sane GitHub Labels](https://medium.com/@dave_lunny/sane-github-labels-c5d2e6004b63) and see [sensible-github-labels](https://github.com/Relequestual/sensible-github-labels) for full descriptions of each
    • “it is much more helpful to see the status and type of all issues at a glance.”
    • One of each:
      • Status: …
        • Abandoned, Accepted, Available, Blocked, Completed, In Progress, On Hold, Pending, Review Needed, Revision Needed
      • Type: …
        • Bug, Maintenance, Question, Enhancement
      • Priority: …
        • Critical, High, Medium, Low
  • [Britecharts](https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/github-labels.html)
    • Status: …
      • On Review – Request that we are pondering if including or not
      • Needs Reproducing – For bugs that need to be reproduced in order to get fixed
      • Needs Design – Feature that needs a design
      • Ready to Go – Issue that has been defined and is ready to get started with
      • In Progress – Issue that is being worked on right now.
      • Completed – Finished feature or fix
    • Type: …
      • Bug – An unexpected problem or unintended behavior
      • Feature – A new feature request
      • Maintenance – A regular maintenance chore or task, including refactors, build system, CI, performance improvements
      • Documentation – A documentation improvement task
      • Question – An issue or PR that needs more information or a user question
    • Not Included
      • Priority: They would add complexity and overhead due to the discussions, but could help with the roadmap
      • Technology Labels: It can create too much overhead, as properly tag with technologies all the issues could be time consuming
  • [Ian Bicking Blog](https://www.ianbicking.org/blog/2014/03/use-github-issues-to-organize-a-project.html)
    • Milestone Overview
      • What are we doing right now?
      • What aren’t we doing right now?
        • 2a. Stuff we’ll probably do soon
        • 2b. Stuff we probably won’t do soon
      • What aren’t we sure about?
    • Milestone Descriptions
      • Stuff we are doing right now: this is the “main” milestone. We give it a name (like Alpha 2 or Strawberry Rhubarb Pie) and we write down what we are trying to accomplish with the milestone. We create a new milestone when we are ready for the next iteration.
      • Stuff we’ll probably do soon: this is a standing “**Next Tasks**” milestone. We never change or rename this milestone.
        • We use a permanent “Next Tasks” milestone (as opposed to renaming it to “Alpha 3” or actual-next-iteration milestone) because we don’t want to presume or default to including something in the real next iteration. When we’re ready to start planning the next iteration we’ll create a new milestone, and only deliberately move things into that milestone.
      • Stuff we probably won’t do soon: this is a standing “**Blue Sky**” milestone. We refer to these tickets and sometimes look through them, but they are easy to ignore, somewhat intentionally ignored.
      • What aren’t we sure about?: issues with no milestone.
    • Label: “Needs Discussion” - (addressed in a triage meeting) - use liberally for either big or small tickets
    • “It’s better to give people more power: it’s actually helpful if people can overreach because it is an opportunity to establish where the limits really are and what purpose those limits have”

docs.title: Constraint satisfaction problems | Combinatorial Optimization Class Notes | Fiveable
docs.text:
Constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) are a powerful framework for modeling complex problems with specific requirements. They involve finding solutions that meet a set of constraints over variables, playing a key role in various optimization scenarios.

CSPs consist of variables, domains, and constraints. Solving techniques include constraint propagation, search algorithms, and local search methods. Advanced concepts like symmetry breaking and global constraints enhance efficiency, while applications span scheduling, resource allocation, and configuration problems.

docs.title: Fundamentals of CSPs
docs.text:
• Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) form a crucial part of Combinatorial Optimization provides a framework for modeling and solving complex problems with constraints
  • CSPs involve finding solutions that satisfy a set of constraints over a set of variables plays a significant role in various optimization scenarios, from scheduling to resource allocation

1 of 3

  • Formal definition of CSPs consists of a set of variables, their domains, and constraints that restrict the values variables can simultaneously take
  • Components include variables (unknowns to be determined), domains (possible values for each variable), and constraints (conditions that must be satisfied)
  • Constraint graph represents the structure of a CSP visually depicts variables as nodes and constraints as edges
  • Solution to a CSP assigns values to all variables while satisfying all constraints

docs.title: Problem representation
docs.text:
• Constraint networks provide a graphical representation of CSPs illustrate relationships between variables and constraints
  • Matrix representation encodes CSP information in a tabular format facilitates efficient constraint checking and propagation
  • Extensional representation explicitly lists all allowed or disallowed combinations of values for constrained variables
  • Intensional representation uses mathematical or logical expressions to define constraints more compact for certain types of problems

docs.title: Constraint types
docs.text:
• Unary constraints involve a single variable restrict the domain of that variable (age must be greater than 18)
  • Binary constraints involve two variables most common type in many CSPs (A must be greater than B)
  • Global constraints involve an arbitrary number of variables express complex relationships efficiently (all-different constraint)
  • Soft constraints express preferences rather than strict requirements allow for optimization in over-constrained problems

docs.title: Variables and domains
docs.text:
• Variables represent the unknowns in the problem can be discrete or continuous
  • Domains define the set of possible values for each variable can be finite (integers, enumerated sets) or infinite (real numbers)
  • Domain reduction techniques narrow down possible values for variables during problem-solving improve efficiency of search algorithms
  • Variable ordering heuristics determine the sequence in which variables are assigned values during search can significantly impact solving speed

docs.title: Constraint propagation techniques
docs.text:
• Constraint propagation forms a fundamental part of solving CSPs efficiently reduces the search space by eliminating inconsistent values
  • These techniques work by enforcing local consistency conditions throughout the constraint network before or during the search process

docs.title: Arc consistency
docs.text:
• Ensures consistency between pairs of variables connected by a constraint removes values from domains that cannot satisfy binary constraints
  • AC-3 algorithm widely used method for achieving arc consistency iteratively revises arcs until no more changes occur
  • Supports early detection of inconsistencies in CSPs can significantly prune the search space before backtracking
  • Time complexity of AC-3 O(ed³) where e number of constraints and d maximum domain size

docs.title: Node consistency
docs.text:
• Simplest form of consistency checking ensures unary constraints are satisfied for each variable
  • Removes values from variable domains that violate unary constraints applied as a preprocessing step before more complex consistency checks
  • Efficiently implemented with a single pass through all variables and their unary constraints
  • Often combined with arc consistency to achieve stronger pruning of the search space

docs.title: Path consistency
docs.text:
• Enforces consistency among triples of variables ensures any consistent assignment to two variables can be extended to a third
  • More powerful than arc consistency but computationally more expensive rarely used in practice due to high time and space complexity
  • PC-2 algorithm common method for achieving path consistency works by revising paths in the constraint graph
  • Can detect inconsistencies missed by arc consistency useful for certain types of temporal reasoning problems

docs.title: K-consistency
docs.text:
• Generalizes the concept of consistency to k variables ensures any consistent assignment to k-1 variables can be extended to the kth
  • Strong k-consistency property achieved when problem is j-consistent for all j ≤ k
  • Computational complexity increases rapidly with k rarely used for k > 3 in practice
  • Theoretical importance in understanding the structure and complexity of CSPs provides insights into problem difficulty

docs.title: Search algorithms for CSPs
docs.text:
• Search algorithms for CSPs aim to find solutions by systematically exploring the space of possible variable assignments
  • These techniques build upon general search algorithms but incorporate CSP-specific heuristics and optimizations to improve efficiency

docs.title: Backtracking search
docs.text:
• Depth-first search algorithm assigns values to variables one at a time backtracks when a constraint violation is detected
  • Variable ordering heuristics choose which variable to assign next (minimum remaining values, degree heuristic)
  • Value ordering heuristics determine the order in which values are tried for a variable (least constraining value)
  • Chronological backtracking simple but can be inefficient in highly constrained problems may revisit the same failed states multiple times

docs.title: Forward checking
docs.text:
• Extends backtracking by checking constraints with unassigned variables after each assignment
  • Maintains arc consistency between the current variable and future variables reduces future backtracking
  • Prunes inconsistent values from the domains of unassigned variables as soon as they become inconsistent
  • More efficient than simple backtracking for many problems but may still perform unnecessary work in highly constrained scenarios

docs.title: Look-ahead techniques
docs.text:
• Full look-ahead (MAC) maintains arc consistency on all constraints after each assignment most powerful general-purpose CSP algorithm
  • Partial look-ahead techniques (forward checking, maintaining arc consistency) balance between pruning and computational cost
  • Variable ordering heuristics particularly effective with look-ahead techniques can significantly reduce the search tree size
  • Dynamic variable ordering adapts the variable selection during search based on the current state of the problem

docs.title: Conflict-directed backjumping
docs.text:
• Improves upon chronological backtracking by jumping back to the source of a conflict rather than the previous variable
  • Maintains a conflict set for each variable records the reasons for failures
  • Reduces redundant search by avoiding revisiting assignments that are known to fail
  • Can be combined with other techniques (forward checking, look-ahead) for even greater efficiency

docs.title: Local search methods
docs.text:
• Local search algorithms for CSPs start with a complete assignment and iteratively improve it by making local changes
  • These methods are particularly useful for large-scale problems where complete search is impractical

docs.title: Min-conflicts algorithm
docs.text:
• Starts with a complete assignment (possibly violating some constraints) iteratively selects a variable and changes its value to minimize conflicts
  • Highly effective for certain types of problems (n-queens) can quickly find solutions for large instances
  • May get stuck in local optima requires restart strategies or other techniques to escape
  • Often used in conjunction with other methods as part of a hybrid approach

docs.title: Tabu search for CSPs
docs.text:
• Extends local search by maintaining a tabu list of recently visited states prevents cycling and encourages exploration of new areas
  • Aspiration criteria allow overriding tabu status for particularly good moves
  • Effective for escaping local optima can find high-quality solutions for difficult problems
  • Requires careful tuning of parameters (tabu list size, aspiration criteria) for optimal performance

docs.title: Simulated annealing in CSPs
docs.text:
• Probabilistic technique for approximating the global optimum of a given function
  • Accepts worse solutions with a probability that decreases over time allows escaping local optima
  • Temperature parameter controls the probability of accepting worse solutions gradually decreased according to a cooling schedule
  • Effective for large, complex CSPs where finding the global optimum is computationally infeasible

docs.title: Constraint optimization problems
docs.text:
• Constraint optimization problems extend CSPs by adding an objective function to be optimized
  • These problems combine the challenges of satisfying constraints with finding the best solution among feasible alternatives

docs.title: Soft constraints vs hard constraints
docs.text:
• Hard constraints must be satisfied for a solution to be valid define the feasible region of the problem
  • Soft constraints express preferences or penalties can be violated but at a cost
  • Modeling with soft constraints allows for more flexible problem formulation captures real-world scenarios more accurately
  • Solving techniques for problems with soft constraints often involve balancing constraint satisfaction with optimization

docs.title: Weighted CSPs
docs.text:
• Assign weights or costs to constraint violations objective is to minimize the total weight of violated constraints
  • Generalizes classical CSPs allows for modeling problems with conflicting objectives
  • Branch and bound algorithms commonly used for solving weighted CSPs prune branches that exceed the current best solution
  • Local search techniques (min-conflicts, tabu search) can be adapted for weighted CSPs by considering constraint weights in the objective function

docs.title: Semiring-based CSPs
docs.text:
• Provides a unified framework for representing and solving various types of CSPs and constraint optimization problems
  • Based on algebraic structures called semirings allows for modeling different types of preferences and constraints
  • Generalizes classical, fuzzy, probabilistic, and weighted CSPs within a single framework
  • Solving techniques for semiring-based CSPs often involve adaptations of classical CSP algorithms to work with the semiring operations

docs.title: Advanced CSP concepts
docs.text:
• Advanced CSP concepts build upon the fundamental techniques to address more complex problem structures and improve solving efficiency
  • These methods often exploit problem-specific properties or leverage sophisticated mathematical tools

docs.title: Symmetry breaking
docs.text:
• Identifies and eliminates symmetric solutions reduces the search space without losing distinct solutions
  • Static symmetry breaking adds constraints to the problem formulation before search begins
  • Dynamic symmetry breaking detects and breaks symmetries during the search process
  • Symmetry detection algorithms identify problem symmetries automatically crucial for complex problems with non-obvious symmetries

docs.title: Global constraints
docs.text:
• Encapsulate complex relationships among a set of variables provide more efficient propagation than equivalent sets of simple constraints
  • Common global constraints include all-different, cardinality, and cumulative constraints
  • Specialized filtering algorithms for global constraints achieve stronger pruning than general-purpose consistency techniques
  • Global constraint catalogs collect and categorize known global constraints facilitate problem modeling and solver implementation

docs.title: Distributed CSPs
docs.text:
• Extension of CSPs where variables and constraints are distributed among multiple agents
  • Applications in multi-agent systems, sensor networks, and distributed scheduling problems
  • Algorithms for DisCSPs include asynchronous backtracking, asynchronous weak commitment search, and distributed breakout
  • Privacy concerns in DisCSPs lead to the development of algorithms that minimize information sharing between agents

docs.title: Applications of CSPs
docs.text:
• CSPs find applications in a wide range of real-world problems across various domains
  • The flexibility of the CSP framework allows for modeling diverse problems with complex constraints

docs.title: Scheduling problems
docs.text:
• Job shop scheduling assigns tasks to machines minimizes makespan or other objectives
  • Timetabling creates schedules for schools, universities, or transportation systems satisfies various constraints (room capacity, teacher availability)
  • Employee rostering assigns shifts to workers considers preferences, qualifications, and labor regulations
  • Project scheduling determines start times for project activities respects precedence constraints and resource limitations

docs.title: Resource allocation
docs.text:
• Frequency assignment in wireless networks assigns frequencies to transmitters minimizes interference
  • Supply chain optimization allocates resources across a network of suppliers, manufacturers, and distributors
  • Cloud computing resource allocation assigns virtual machines to physical servers optimizes performance and energy efficiency
  • Portfolio optimization allocates financial resources across different investments balances risk and return

docs.title: Configuration problems
docs.text:
• Product configuration determines valid combinations of product features satisfies customer requirements and manufacturing constraints
  • Network configuration sets up network devices and connections ensures proper functionality and security
  • Software configuration management manages dependencies between software components ensures consistent and valid configurations

docs.title: Temporal reasoning
docs.text:
• Planning and scheduling with temporal constraints reasons about durations and deadlines

  • Temporal constraint networks represent and reason about qualitative and quantitative temporal relations

  • Medical treatment planning schedules treatments respecting temporal constraints between procedures

  • Logistics and transportation scheduling coordinates deliveries and pickups satisfies time windows and precedence constraints

  • CSP solvers and tools provide implementations of various algorithms and techniques for modeling and solving CSPs

  • These tools range from low-level libraries to high-level modeling languages and integrated development environments

docs.title: Popular CSP libraries
docs.text:
• Gecode open-source C++ library for developing constraint-based systems and applications
  • OR-Tools Google’s suite of optimization tools includes CSP solver along with other optimization algorithms
  • Choco Java library for constraint programming and constraint-based local search
  • MiniZinc constraint modeling language and toolchain supports various backend solvers

docs.title: Modeling languages for CSPs
docs.text:
• AMPL algebraic modeling language for mathematical programming problems including CSPs
  • OPL IBM’s Optimization Programming Language designed for modeling optimization problems
  • Essence abstract constraint specification language allows high-level problem descriptions
  • XCSP3 XML-based format for representing constraint satisfaction and optimization problems

docs.title: Benchmarking and evaluation
docs.text:
• CSPLib collection of CSP problem instances used for benchmarking and comparing algorithms
  • XCSP3 competitions evaluate and compare CSP solvers on standardized problem sets
  • Performance metrics include runtime, number of backtracks, and solution quality
  • Visualization tools help analyze solver behavior and problem structure aid in algorithm development and tuning

docs.title: Complexity and tractability
docs.text:
• Understanding the complexity of CSPs is crucial for developing efficient solving strategies and recognizing tractable problem classes
  • Complexity analysis provides insights into the fundamental difficulty of different types of CSPs

docs.title: Complexity classes of CSPs
docs.text:

def detect_input_format(data: dict[str, Any] | str) -> str:
    """Detect input format from data structure.

    Args:
        data: JSON data dictionary or string content

    Returns:
        Format name ('svg', 'obsidian', 'tldraw', or 'excalidraw')

    Raises:
        ValueError: If format cannot be detected
    """
    # Check if it's string content (SVG, Obsidian Excalidraw markdown, PlantUML, or Mermaid)
    if isinstance(data, str):
        if data.strip().startswith('<?xml') or data.strip().startswith('<svg'):
            return 'svg'
        if is_obsidian_excalidraw(data):
            return 'obsidian'
        if is_plantuml(data):
            return 'plantuml'
        if is_mermaid(data):
            return 'mermaid'
        raise ValueError('Unknown string format - expected SVG XML, Obsidian Excalidraw markdown, PlantUML, or Mermaid')

    # Modern TLDraw v2 .tldr files have "tldrawFileFormatVersion" + flat "records"
    if is_tldraw_v2(data):
        return 'tldraw'

    # Legacy TLDraw has "document" -> "pages" structure
    if 'document' in data and 'pages' in data.get('document', {}):
        return 'tldraw'

    # Excalidraw has "elements" or "type": "excalidraw/clipboard"
    if 'elements' in data or data.get('type') == 'excalidraw/clipboard':
        return 'excalidraw'

    raise ValueError('Unknown input format - expected SVG, TLDraw, or Excalidraw')

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Main CLI entry point.

    Dispatches to the `formats`, `inspect`, or `convert` subcommands. For
    backward compatibility, bare conversion invocations without a subcommand
    (`diacea -i file -f mermaid`) are treated as `convert`.

    Args:
        argv: Command-line arguments (None = sys.argv)

    Returns:
        Exit code (0 = success, 1 = error, 2 = parsed 0 elements)
    """
    args_list = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    match args_list:
        case ['convert', *rest]:
            return _run_convert(rest)
        case ['formats', *rest]:
            return _run_formats(rest)
        case ['inspect', *rest]:
            return _run_inspect(rest)
        case ['sync', *rest]:
            return _run_sync(rest)
        case _:
            return _run_convert(args_list)

Registers a DiagramView per entry (creating it if absent), extracts labeled shapes with their inferred semantic types into shared ElementDefinition entries, and records the element IDs each view uses.

Elements are de-duplicated by normalized label (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed). When the same label appears with conflicting semantic types, the higher-confidence inference wins (first-wins on ties) and the conflict is recorded in the summary warnings.

def ingest_diagrams(
    workspace: Workspace,
    diagram_files: dict[str, tuple[str, str]],
) -> IngestionSummary:
    """Parse diagram files and populate the workspace element library.

    Registers a DiagramView per entry (creating it if absent), extracts labeled
    shapes with their inferred semantic types into shared ElementDefinition
    entries, and records the element IDs each view uses.

    Elements are de-duplicated by normalized label (case-insensitive,
    whitespace-collapsed). When the same label appears with conflicting
    semantic types, the higher-confidence inference wins (first-wins on ties)
    and the conflict is recorded in the summary warnings.

    Args:
        workspace: Workspace to populate in place
        diagram_files: Mapping of view ID to (file_path, view_type)

    Returns:
        IngestionSummary with counts and conflict warnings

    Raises:
        DiagramIngestionError: If a diagram file is missing or unparseable
    """
    summary = IngestionSummary()
    elements_by_name: dict[str, ElementDefinition] = {
        _normalize_name(elem.label): elem for elem in workspace.elements.values()
    }

    for view_id, (file_path, view_type) in diagram_files.items():
        diagram = parse_diagram_file(file_path)
        summary.diagrams_parsed += 1

        element_refs: list[str] = []
        for shape in diagram.get_shapes():
            normalized = _normalize_name(shape.label)
            if not normalized:
                continue

            semantic_type = _semantic_type_name(shape.semantic_type)
            confidence = shape.semantic_confidence

            existing = elements_by_name.get(normalized)
            if existing is None:
                element = ElementDefinition(
                    id=_slugify(normalized),
                    label=_collapse_whitespace(shape.label),
                    element_type=semantic_type,
                    metadata={
                        'semantic_confidence': confidence,
                        'source_file': str(file_path),
                    },
                )
                workspace.add_element(element)
                elements_by_name[normalized] = element
                summary.elements_added += 1
                element_id = element.id
            else:
                summary.deduplicated += 1
                element_id = existing.id
                if existing.element_type != semantic_type:
                    _resolve_type_conflict(existing, semantic_type, confidence, file_path, summary)

            if element_id not in element_refs:
                element_refs.append(element_id)

        view = workspace.views.get(view_id)
        if view is None:
            view = DiagramView(
                id=view_id,
                name=view_id.replace('-', ' ').replace('_', ' ').title(),
                view_type=view_type,
                file=str(file_path),
            )
            workspace.add_view(view)
        view.element_refs = element_refs

    return summary

def parse_diagram_file(file_path: str | Path) -> Diagram:
    """Parse a diagram file to IR using format auto-detection.

    Raises:
        DiagramIngestionError: If the file is missing, its format cannot be
            detected, or parsing fails.
    """
    path = Path(file_path)
    if not path.exists():
        msg = f'Diagram file not found: {path}'
        raise DiagramIngestionError(msg)

    content = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    stripped = content.strip()

    if stripped.startswith(('<?xml', '<svg')):
        input_format = 'svg'
        input_data: dict[str, Any] | str = content
    else:
        try:
            input_format = detect_input_format(content)
            input_data = content
        except ValueError:
            try:
                input_data = json.loads(content)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as err:
                msg = (
                    f"Could not detect diagram format of '{path}': not SVG, "
                    f'Obsidian Excalidraw markdown, PlantUML, Mermaid, or valid JSON'
                )
                raise DiagramIngestionError(msg) from err
            try:
                input_format = detect_input_format(input_data)
            except ValueError as err:
                msg = f"Could not detect diagram format of '{path}': {err}"
                raise DiagramIngestionError(msg) from err

    try:
        if input_format == 'svg':
            return SVGParser().parse(input_data)
        if input_format == 'obsidian':
            if not isinstance(input_data, str):
                msg = f"Obsidian Excalidraw requires text content: '{path}'"
                raise DiagramIngestionError(msg)
            return ExcalidrawParser().parse(extract_excalidraw_json(input_data))
        if input_format == 'mermaid':
            return MermaidParser().parse(input_data)
        if input_format == 'plantuml':
            return PlantUMLParser().parse(input_data)
        if input_format == 'tldraw':
            return TLDrawParser().parse(input_data)
        return ExcalidrawParser().parse(input_data)
    except ValueError as err:
        msg = f"Failed to parse diagram '{path}': {err}"
        raise DiagramIngestionError(msg) from err

def view_id_from_path(file_path: str | Path) -> str:
    """Derive a view ID from a diagram file name (e.g. 'a.excalidraw.md' -> 'a')."""
    name = Path(file_path).name
    known_suffixes = ('.md', '.mmd', '.excalidraw', '.puml', '.tldr', '.json', '.svg')
    while name.lower().endswith(known_suffixes):
        name = name[: name.rfind('.')]
    return _slugify(name.lower())

def replace_diacea_fences(markdown: str, base_dirs: Sequence[str | Path]) -> str:
    """Replace every ```diacea fence with a generated diagram code block."""

    def _render(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        indent = match.group('indent')
        options = _parse_fence_body(match.group('body'))
        source = _resolve_source(options['source'], base_dirs)
        try:
            diagram = parse_diagram_file(source)
        except DiagramIngestionError as err:
            raise DiaceaFenceError(str(err)) from err
        output = _generate(diagram, options['format'], options.get('mermaid-type'))
        language = _FENCE_LANGUAGES[options['format']]
        lines = [f'{indent}```{language}']
        lines.extend(f'{indent}{line}'.rstrip() for line in output.splitlines())
        lines.append(f'{indent}```')
        return '\n'.join(lines)

    return _FENCE_RE.sub(_render, markdown)

def workspace_create(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Create a new workspace by ingesting diagram files.

    Args:
        args: Command-line arguments

    Returns:
        Exit code
    """
    # Parse diagram file specifications
    diagram_files: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}

    for spec in args.add:
        # Format: file_path:view_id:view_type or file_path:view_id
        parts = _split_diagram_spec(spec)
        if len(parts) < 2:
            print(f"Error: Invalid diagram spec '{spec}' (use file:view_id or file:view_id:type)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        file_path = parts[0]
        view_id = parts[1]
        view_type = parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else 'diagram'

        diagram_files[view_id] = (file_path, view_type)

    for file_path in args.from_diagrams or []:
        view_id = view_id_from_path(file_path)
        if view_id in diagram_files:
            print(f"Error: Duplicate view ID '{view_id}' derived from '{file_path}'", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        diagram_files[view_id] = (file_path, 'diagram')

    # Create workspace (parses each diagram file and extracts elements)
    try:
        workspace, summary = create_workspace_from_diagrams(
            workspace_id=args.id or args.name.lower().replace(' ', '-'),
            workspace_name=args.name,
            diagram_files=diagram_files,
        )
    except DiagramIngestionError as err:
        print(f'Error: {err}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    workspace.description = args.description or ''
    workspace.author = args.author or ''

    # Save workspace
    format_type = 'yaml' if args.output.endswith(('.yml', '.yaml')) else 'json'
    save_workspace(workspace, args.output, format=format_type)

def load_workspace(file_path: str | Path) -> Workspace:
    """Load workspace from YAML or JSON file.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to workspace file (.yml, .yaml, or .json)

    Returns:
        Workspace object

    Raises:
        ValueError: If file format is not supported
        FileNotFoundError: If file doesn't exist
    """
    path = Path(file_path)
    if not path.exists():
        msg = f'Workspace file not found: {file_path}'
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)

    content = Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8')

    # Detect format from extension
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in {'.yml', '.yaml'}:
        data = yaml.safe_load(content)
    elif suffix == '.json':
        data = json.loads(content)
    else:
        msg = f'Unsupported workspace format: {suffix} (use .yml, .yaml, or .json)'
        raise ValueError(msg)

    return from_dict(data)

def save_workspace(workspace: Workspace, file_path: str | Path, format: str = 'yaml') -> None:  # noqa: A002
    """Save workspace to YAML or JSON file.

    Args:
        workspace: Workspace object to save
        file_path: Output file path
        format: Output format ("yaml" or "json")

    Raises:
        ValueError: If format is not supported
    """
    data = to_dict(workspace)

    path = Path(file_path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with Path(path).open('w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        if format == 'yaml':
            yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False)
        elif format == 'json':
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        else:
            msg = f"Unsupported format: {format} (use 'yaml' or 'json')"
            raise ValueError(msg)

class D2Generator(Generator):
    """Generate D2 from IR."""

    def __init__(self, config: D2Config | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize generator.

        Args:
            config: D2 configuration or None for defaults
        """
        self.config = config or D2Config()
        self._element_paths: dict[str, str] = {}  # id -> D2 path

    def generate(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate D2 diagram from IR.

        Args:
            diagram: IR Diagram object

        Returns:
            D2 diagram string
        """
        lines: list[str] = []

        # Direction
        direction = self.config.direction or self._detect_direction(diagram)
        if direction:
            lines.extend((f'direction: {direction}', ''))

        # Build element paths for hierarchy
        self._build_element_paths(diagram)

        # Generate all elements
        self._write_elements(diagram, lines)

        # Generate connections
        connections = [conn for conn in diagram.get_connections() if not self._is_ancestor_connection(conn)]
        if connections:
            lines.append('')
            lines.extend(self._format_connection(conn) for conn in connections)

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _is_ancestor_connection(self, conn: Connection) -> bool:
        """Detect connections between a container and its own descendant.

        d2's dagre layout rejects them, so they are dropped with a warning.
        """
        from_path = self._element_paths.get(conn.from_id, self._sanitize_id(conn.from_id))
        to_path = self._element_paths.get(conn.to_id, self._sanitize_id(conn.to_id))
        if to_path.startswith(f'{from_path}.') or from_path.startswith(f'{to_path}.'):
            warnings.warn(
                f'Dropping connection between container and its descendant: {from_path} -> {to_path}',
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            return True
        return False

    def _detect_direction(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str | None:
        """Auto-detect optimal direction based on layout."""
        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        if not shapes:
            return None

        # Calculate bounding box
        min_x = min(s.position.x for s in shapes)
        max_x = max(s.position.x + s.size.width for s in shapes)
        min_y = min(s.position.y for s in shapes)
        max_y = max(s.position.y + s.size.height for s in shapes)

        width = max_x - min_x
        height = max_y - min_y

        # If wider than tall, use right
        if width > height * 1.5:
            return 'right'
        # If taller than wide, use down
        if height > width * 1.5:
            return 'down'

        return None  # Let D2 decide

    def _build_element_paths(self, diagram: Diagram) -> None:
        """Build D2 paths for all elements."""
        self._element_paths.clear()

        # Map elements to their groups
        child_to_parent: dict[str, str] = {}
        groups = diagram.get_groups()

        for group in groups:
            for child_id in group.children:
                child_to_parent[child_id] = group.id

        # Build paths recursively
        def get_path(elem_id: str, visited: set[str]) -> str:
            if elem_id in visited:
                # Circular reference, just use sanitized ID
                return self._sanitize_id(elem_id)

            visited.add(elem_id)

            if elem_id in child_to_parent:
                parent_id = child_to_parent[elem_id]
                parent_path = get_path(parent_id, visited)
                sanitized_id = self._sanitize_id(elem_id)
                return f'{parent_path}.{sanitized_id}' if parent_path else sanitized_id
            return self._sanitize_id(elem_id)

        for elem in diagram.elements:
            self._element_paths[elem.id] = get_path(elem.id, set())

        for group in groups:
            source_id = group.source_shape_id
            if source_id != group.id and source_id not in child_to_parent:
                self._element_paths[source_id] = self._element_paths.get(group.id, self._sanitize_id(group.id))

    def _write_elements(self, diagram: Diagram, lines: list[str]) -> None:
        """Write all elements (shapes and groups)."""
        groups = diagram.get_groups()
        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()

        shapes_by_id = {s.id: s for s in shapes}
        groups_by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
        for group in top_level_groups(groups):
            self._write_group(group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, lines)

        grouped_ids = set()
        for group in groups:
            grouped_ids.update(group.children)

        group_source_ids = {g.source_shape_id for g in groups}
        standalone_shapes = [s for s in shapes if s.id not in grouped_ids and s.id not in group_source_ids]
        lines.extend(self._format_shape(shape) for shape in standalone_shapes)

    def _write_group(
        self,
        group: Group,
        shapes_by_id: dict[str, Shape],
        groups_by_id: dict[str, Group],
        lines: list[str],
    ) -> None:
        """Write a group as a D2 container, recursing into child groups."""
        group_id = self._sanitize_id(group.id)
        label = self._escape_label(group.label or group_id)

        lines.append(f'{group_id}: {label} {{')

        for child_id in group.children:
            child_group = groups_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_group:
                nested_lines: list[str] = []
                self._write_group(child_group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, nested_lines)
                lines.extend(f'  {line}' if line else line for line in nested_lines)
                continue
            child_shape = shapes_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_shape:
                child_line = self._format_shape(child_shape, use_relative_path=True)
                lines.extend(f'  {line}' for line in child_line.split('\n'))

        lines.extend(('}', ''))

    def _format_shape(self, shape: Shape, use_relative_path: bool = False) -> str:
        """Format a D2 shape declaration."""
        if use_relative_path:
            shape_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        else:
            shape_id = self._element_paths.get(shape.id, self._sanitize_id(shape.id))

        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or shape_id)

        # Determine D2 shape
        d2_shape = self._get_d2_shape(shape)
        has_style = self._has_custom_style(shape)

        # Simple declaration if no special properties
        if not d2_shape and not has_style:
            return f'{shape_id}: {label}'

        # Complex declaration with properties
        lines = [f'{shape_id}: {label} {{']

        if d2_shape:
            lines.append(f'  shape: {d2_shape}')

        if has_style:
            style_lines = self._format_style(shape)
            lines.extend(f'  {line}' for line in style_lines)

        lines.append('}')

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _get_d2_shape(self, shape: Shape) -> str | None:
        """Get D2 shape name based on semantic or geometric type."""
        # Check semantic type first
        if shape.semantic_type and shape.semantic_type in self.config.shape_map:
            return self.config.shape_map[shape.semantic_type]

        # Map geometric shapes
        shape_map = {
            'ellipse': 'oval',
            'diamond': 'diamond',
            'circle': 'circle',
        }

        return shape_map.get(shape.shape_type)

    def _has_custom_style(self, shape: Shape) -> bool:
        """Check if shape has custom styling."""
        style = shape.style
        return bool(style.fill_color or style.stroke_color or style.stroke_width or style.stroke_style == 'dashed')

    def _format_style(self, shape: Shape) -> list[str]:
        """Format D2 style block for a shape."""
        lines = []
        style = shape.style

        style_props = []
        if style.fill_color:
            style_props.append(f'fill: "{style.fill_color}"')

        if style.stroke_color:
            style_props.append(f'stroke: "{style.stroke_color}"')

        if style.stroke_width:
            style_props.append(f'stroke-width: {int(style.stroke_width)}')

        if style.stroke_style == 'dashed':
            style_props.append('stroke-dash: 3')

        if style_props:
            lines.append('style: {')
            lines.extend(f'  {prop}' for prop in style_props)
            lines.append('}')

        return lines

    def _format_connection(self, conn: Connection) -> str:
        """Format a D2 connection."""
        from_path = self._element_paths.get(conn.from_id, self._sanitize_id(conn.from_id))
        to_path = self._element_paths.get(conn.to_id, self._sanitize_id(conn.to_id))

        # Determine arrow type
        arrow = self._get_arrow_type(conn)

        # Format connection
        if conn.label:
            label = self._escape_label(conn.label)
            line = f'{from_path} {arrow} {to_path}: {label}'
        else:
            line = f'{from_path} {arrow} {to_path}'

        # Add styling if needed
        if self._connection_has_style(conn):
            lines = [line + ' {']
            style_lines = self._format_connection_style(conn)
            lines.extend(f'  {style_line}' for style_line in style_lines)
            lines.append('}')
            return '\n'.join(lines)

        return line

    def _get_arrow_type(self, conn: Connection) -> str:
        """Get D2 arrow type."""
        if conn.connection_type == 'bidirectional':
            return '<->'
        return '->'

    def _connection_has_style(self, conn: Connection) -> bool:
        """Check if connection has custom styling."""
        style = conn.style
        return bool(style.stroke_color or style.stroke_width or style.stroke_style == 'dashed')

    def _format_connection_style(self, conn: Connection) -> list[str]:
        """Format D2 style for connection."""
        lines = []
        style = conn.style

        style_props = []
        if style.stroke_color:
            style_props.append(f'stroke: "{style.stroke_color}"')

        if style.stroke_width:
            style_props.append(f'stroke-width: {int(style.stroke_width)}')

        if style.stroke_style == 'dashed':
            style_props.append('stroke-dash: 3')

        if style_props:
            lines.append('style: {')
            lines.extend(f'  {prop}' for prop in style_props)
            lines.append('}')

        return lines

    def _sanitize_id(self, id_str: str) -> str:
        """Sanitize ID for D2 format."""
        # D2 allows hyphens and underscores
        # Replace spaces and special chars
        sanitized = id_str.replace(' ', '_').replace(':', '_')

        # Escape if starts with number
        if sanitized and sanitized[0].isdigit():
            sanitized = 'n_' + sanitized

        return sanitized or 'node'

    def _escape_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Escape label for D2 format."""
        # D2 handles most characters well, escape special ones
        escaped = label.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('\n', '\\n')

        # Quote if contains special characters
        if any(c in escaped for c in ['{', '}', ':', ';']):
            escaped = f'"{escaped}"'

        return escaped

class GraphVizGenerator(Generator):
    """Generate GraphViz DOT from IR."""

    def __init__(self, config: GraphVizConfig | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize generator.

        Args:
            config: GraphViz configuration or None for defaults
        """
        self.config = config or GraphVizConfig()

    def generate(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate DOT file from IR.

        Args:
            diagram: IR Diagram object

        Returns:
            GraphViz DOT string
        """
        lines = []

        # Determine direction
        direction = self.config.direction or self._detect_direction(diagram)

        # Header
        graph_type = self.config.graph_type
        lines.append(f'{graph_type} "{diagram.name or "diagram"}" {{')

        # Graph attributes
        if direction:
            lines.append(f'    rankdir="{direction}";')

        lines.extend(('    node [fontname="Helvetica"];', '    edge [fontname="Helvetica"];', ''))

        # Process groups as clusters
        groups = diagram.get_groups()
        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()

        if self.config.use_clusters and groups:
            shapes_by_id = {s.id: s for s in shapes}
            groups_by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
            for group in top_level_groups(groups):
                self._write_cluster(group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, lines, depth=1)
            lines.append('')

        # Process standalone nodes (not in clusters)
        standalone_shapes = self._get_standalone_shapes(shapes, groups)
        lines.extend(self._format_node(shape) for shape in standalone_shapes)

        if standalone_shapes:
            lines.append('')

        # Process connections
        lines.extend(self._format_edge(conn) for conn in connections)

        # Footer
        lines.append('}')

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _detect_direction(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Auto-detect optimal rankdir based on diagram layout.

        Returns LR (horizontal) or TB (vertical) based on aspect ratio.
        """
        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        if not shapes:
            return 'LR'  # Default

        # Calculate bounding box
        min_x = min(s.position.x for s in shapes)
        max_x = max(s.position.x + s.size.width for s in shapes)
        min_y = min(s.position.y for s in shapes)
        max_y = max(s.position.y + s.size.height for s in shapes)

        width = max_x - min_x
        height = max_y - min_y

        # If significantly wider than tall, use LR
        if width > height * 1.5:
            return 'LR'
        # If significantly taller than wide, use TB
        if height > width * 1.5:
            return 'TB'

        return 'LR'  # Default horizontal

    def _get_standalone_shapes(self, shapes: list[Shape], groups: list[Group]) -> list[Shape]:
        """Get shapes that are not in any group and haven't become groups."""
        grouped_ids = set()
        for group in groups:
            grouped_ids.update(group.children)

        group_source_ids = {g.source_shape_id for g in groups}
        return [s for s in shapes if s.id not in grouped_ids and s.id not in group_source_ids]

    def _write_cluster(
        self,
        group: Group,
        shapes_by_id: dict[str, Shape],
        groups_by_id: dict[str, Group],
        lines: list[str],
        depth: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Write a cluster (subgraph) for a group, recursing into child groups."""
        if depth > self.config.max_cluster_depth:
            warnings.warn(
                f'group {group.id!r} exceeds max cluster depth {self.config.max_cluster_depth}; truncating',
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            return

        indent = '    ' * depth
        cluster_id = self._sanitize_id(group.id)
        label = self._escape_label(group.label or cluster_id)

        lines.extend(
            (f'{indent}subgraph {self.config.cluster_prefix}{cluster_id} {{', f'{indent}    label="{label}";')
        )

        for child_id in group.children:
            child_group = groups_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_group:
                self._write_cluster(child_group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, lines, depth + 1)
                continue
            child = shapes_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child:
                lines.append(self._format_node(child, indent=indent + '    '))

        lines.append(f'{indent}}}')

    def _format_node(self, shape: Shape, indent: str = '    ') -> str:
        """Format a GraphViz node."""
        node_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or node_id)

        # Determine node shape
        node_shape = self._get_node_shape(shape)

        # Build attribute list
        attrs = [f'label="{label}"']

        if node_shape != 'box':  # box is default
            attrs.append(f'shape="{node_shape}"')

        # Add styling
        if shape.style.fill_color:
            attrs.extend((f'fillcolor="{shape.style.fill_color}"', 'style="filled"'))

        if shape.style.stroke_color:
            attrs.append(f'color="{shape.style.stroke_color}"')

        if shape.style.stroke_width:
            attrs.append(f'penwidth="{shape.style.stroke_width}"')

        # Join attributes
        attr_str = ', '.join(attrs)
        return f'{indent}{node_id} [{attr_str}];'

    def _get_node_shape(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Get GraphViz node shape based on semantic or geometric type."""
        # Check semantic type first
        if shape.semantic_type and shape.semantic_type in self.config.node_shape_map:
            return self.config.node_shape_map[shape.semantic_type]

        # Fallback to geometric shape
        shape_map = {
            'rectangle': 'box',
            'ellipse': 'ellipse',
            'diamond': 'diamond',
            'circle': 'circle',
        }

        return shape_map.get(shape.shape_type, 'box')

    def _format_edge(self, conn: Connection) -> str:
        """Format a GraphViz edge."""
        from_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.from_id)
        to_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.to_id)

        # Determine arrow type
        dir_attr = None
        if self.config.graph_type == 'graph':  # Undirected
            arrow = '--'
        elif conn.connection_type == 'bidirectional':
            arrow = '->'
            dir_attr = 'dir="both"'
        else:
            arrow = '->'

        # Build attribute list
        attrs = []

        if conn.label:
            label = self._escape_label(conn.label)
            attrs.append(f'label="{label}"')

        if conn.style.stroke_style == 'dashed':
            attrs.append('style="dashed"')

        if conn.style.stroke_color:
            attrs.append(f'color="{conn.style.stroke_color}"')

        if conn.style.stroke_width:
            attrs.append(f'penwidth="{conn.style.stroke_width}"')

        if dir_attr:
            attrs.append(dir_attr)

        # Format edge
        if attrs:
            attr_str = ', '.join(attrs)
            return f'    {from_id} {arrow} {to_id} [{attr_str}];'

        return f'    {from_id} {arrow} {to_id};'

    def _sanitize_id(self, id_str: str) -> str:
        """Sanitize ID for DOT format."""
        # Replace invalid characters
        sanitized = id_str.replace('-', '_').replace(':', '_').replace(' ', '_')

        # Ensure starts with letter or underscore
        if sanitized and not (sanitized[0].isalpha() or sanitized[0] == '_'):
            sanitized = 'n_' + sanitized

        return sanitized or 'node'

    def _escape_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Escape label for DOT format."""
        # Escape backslashes and quotes
        return label.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"').replace('\n', '\\n')

class MermaidGenerator(Generator):
    """Generate Mermaid diagrams from IR with auto-detection."""

    def __init__(self, diagram_type: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize generator.

        Args:
            diagram_type: Force specific type ('flowchart', 'c4', 'sequence')
                         or None for auto-detection
        """
        self.diagram_type = diagram_type
        self.detected_type: str | None = None
        self.max_subgraph_depth = 3

    def generate(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate Mermaid diagram from IR.

        Args:
            diagram: IR Diagram object

        Returns:
            Mermaid diagram string
        """
        # Auto-detect diagram type if not specified
        diagram_type = self.diagram_type or self._detect_diagram_type(diagram)
        self.detected_type = diagram_type

        if diagram_type == 'c4':
            return self._generate_c4(diagram)
        if diagram_type == 'sequence':
            return self._generate_sequence(diagram)
        # flowchart (default)  # noqa: ERA001
        return self._generate_flowchart(diagram)

    def _detect_diagram_type(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Auto-detect best Mermaid diagram type.

        Detection logic:
        - If has Person/System/Container semantic types → C4
        - If connections form sequential flow → Sequence
        - Default → Flowchart

        A parser-provided ``metadata["mermaid"]["diagram_type"]`` wins over
        the heuristics.
        """
        source_type = diagram.metadata.get('mermaid', {}).get('diagram_type')
        if source_type in {'c4', 'flowchart', 'sequence'}:
            return source_type

        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()

        # Check for C4 semantic types
        c4_types = {
            SemanticType.PERSON,
            SemanticType.SYSTEM,
            SemanticType.CONTAINER,
            SemanticType.COMPONENT,
        }

        semantic_types = {s.semantic_type for s in shapes if s.semantic_type}

        if semantic_types & c4_types:  # Intersection
            return 'c4'

        # Check for sequential pattern (each shape has at most one out connection)
        # This is a simple heuristic - could be improved
        out_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        for conn in connections:
            out_counts[conn.from_id] = out_counts.get(conn.from_id, 0) + 1

        if connections and all(count <= 1 for count in out_counts.values()):
            return 'sequence'

        # Default to flowchart
        return 'flowchart'

    def _generate_flowchart(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate Mermaid flowchart."""
        lines = ['flowchart LR']  # Left-to-right by default

        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()
        groups = diagram.get_groups()

        group_source_ids = {g.source_shape_id for g in groups}
        child_ids = {child_id for g in groups for child_id in g.children}
        top_level_shapes = [s for s in shapes if s.id not in child_ids and s.id not in group_source_ids]

        lines.extend(self._format_flowchart_node(shape) for shape in top_level_shapes)

        shapes_by_id = {s.id: s for s in shapes}
        groups_by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
        for group in top_level_groups(groups):
            subgraph_lines = self._generate_subgraph(group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, depth=1)
            lines.extend(subgraph_lines)

        # Generate connections
        lines.extend(self._format_flowchart_connection(conn) for conn in connections)

        # Add styling (basic colors)
        style_lines = self._generate_flowchart_styles(shapes)
        if style_lines:
            lines.append('')
            lines.extend(style_lines)

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _format_flowchart_node(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Format a Mermaid flowchart node."""
        node_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._format_bracket_label(shape.label or node_id)
        brackets = self._get_node_brackets(shape)
        return f'    {node_id}{brackets[0]}{label}{brackets[1]}'

    def _format_bracket_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        escaped = self._escape_label(label)
        if _LABEL_CHARS_REQUIRING_QUOTES & set(label):
            return f'"{escaped}"'
        return escaped

    def _get_node_brackets(self, shape: Shape) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Get Mermaid node brackets based on shape type.

        Returns tuple of (opening, closing) brackets.
        """
        # Check semantic type first
        if shape.semantic_type:
            semantic = shape.semantic_type
            if semantic == SemanticType.DECISION:
                return ('{', '}')  # Diamond
            if semantic == SemanticType.DATABASE:
                return ('[(', ')]')  # Cylindrical
            if semantic == SemanticType.PERSON:
                return ('([', '])')  # Stadium/rounded
            if semantic == SemanticType.START_END:
                return ('([', '])')  # Stadium

        # Fall back to geometric shape
        shape_map = {
            'rectangle': ('[', ']'),
            'ellipse': ('([', '])'),
            'diamond': ('{', '}'),
            'circle': ('((', '))'),
        }

        return shape_map.get(shape.shape_type, ('[', ']'))  # Default rectangle

    def _format_flowchart_connection(self, conn: Connection) -> str:
        """Format a Mermaid flowchart connection."""
        from_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.from_id)
        to_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.to_id)

        # Determine arrow style
        if conn.connection_type == 'bidirectional':
            arrow = '<-->'
        elif conn.style.stroke_style == 'dashed':
            arrow = '-.->'
        else:
            arrow = '-->'

        if conn.label:
            label = self._escape_pipe_label(conn.label)
            return f'    {from_id} {arrow}|{label}| {to_id}'
        return f'    {from_id} {arrow} {to_id}'

    def _generate_subgraph(
        self,
        group: Group,
        shapes_by_id: dict[str, Shape],
        groups_by_id: dict[str, Group],
        depth: int,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Generate Mermaid subgraph for a group, recursing into child groups."""
        if depth > self.max_subgraph_depth:
            warnings.warn(
                f'group {group.id!r} exceeds max subgraph depth {self.max_subgraph_depth}; truncating',
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            return []

        lines = []
        indent = '    ' * depth
        subgraph_id = self._sanitize_id(group.id)
        label = self._format_bracket_label(group.label or subgraph_id)
        lines.append(f'{indent}subgraph {subgraph_id}[{label}]')

        for child_id in group.children:
            child_group = groups_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_group:
                lines.extend(self._generate_subgraph(child_group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, depth + 1))
                continue
            child_shape = shapes_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_shape:
                node_line = self._format_flowchart_node(child_shape)
                lines.append(indent + node_line)

        lines.append(f'{indent}end')
        return lines

    def _generate_flowchart_styles(self, shapes: list[Shape]) -> list[str]:
        """Generate Mermaid style definitions for shapes."""
        lines = []

        for shape in shapes:
            if not shape.style.fill_color and not shape.style.stroke_color:
                continue  # No custom styling

            node_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
            style_parts = []

            if shape.style.fill_color:
                style_parts.append(f'fill:{shape.style.fill_color}')

            if shape.style.stroke_color:
                style_parts.append(f'stroke:{shape.style.stroke_color}')

            if style_parts:
                style_str = ','.join(style_parts)
                lines.append(f'    style {node_id} {style_str}')

        return lines

    def _generate_c4(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate Mermaid C4 diagram."""
        lines = ['C4Context']  # Start with Context level
        lines.append('    title ' + (diagram.name or 'Architecture Diagram'))

        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()
        groups = diagram.get_groups()

        group_source_ids = {g.source_shape_id for g in groups}
        child_ids = {cid for g in groups for cid in g.children}
        shapes_by_id = {s.id: s for s in shapes}
        groups_by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
        declared_ids: set[str] = set()
        group_representatives: dict[str, str] = {}

        for shape in shapes:
            if shape.id in child_ids or shape.id in group_source_ids:
                continue
            if shape.id in declared_ids:
                continue
            lines.append(self._format_c4_element(shape, in_boundary=False))
            declared_ids.add(shape.id)

        for group in top_level_groups(groups):
            lines.extend(
                self._generate_c4_boundary(group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, declared_ids, group_representatives)
            )

        for shape in shapes:
            if shape.id in declared_ids or shape.id in group_source_ids:
                continue
            lines.append(self._format_c4_element(shape, in_boundary=False))
            declared_ids.add(shape.id)

        source_to_group = {g.source_shape_id: g.id for g in groups}
        for conn in connections:
            rel_line = self._format_c4_rel(conn, declared_ids, source_to_group, group_representatives)
            if rel_line:
                lines.append(rel_line)

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _generate_c4_boundary(
        self,
        group: Group,
        shapes_by_id: dict[str, Shape],
        groups_by_id: dict[str, Group],
        declared_ids: set[str],
        group_representatives: dict[str, str],
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Generate a C4 boundary, recursing into child groups and skipping empty groups."""
        body: list[str] = []
        for child_id in group.children:
            child_group = groups_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_group:
                body.extend(
                    self._generate_c4_boundary(
                        child_group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, declared_ids, group_representatives
                    )
                )
                if child_group.id in group_representatives:
                    group_representatives.setdefault(group.id, group_representatives[child_group.id])
                continue
            child_shape = shapes_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_shape and child_shape.id not in declared_ids:
                body.append(self._format_c4_element(child_shape, in_boundary=True))
                declared_ids.add(child_shape.id)
                group_representatives.setdefault(group.id, child_shape.id)

        if not body:
            warnings.warn(f'group {group.id!r} has no resolvable children; skipping empty C4 boundary', stacklevel=2)
            return []

        label = self._escape_quoted_label(group.label or group.source_shape_id)
        boundary_id = self._sanitize_id(group.id)
        return [f'    Boundary({boundary_id}, "{label}") {{', *body, '    }']

    def _format_c4_rel(
        self,
        conn: Connection,
        declared_ids: set[str],
        source_to_group: dict[str, str],
        group_representatives: dict[str, str],
    ) -> str | None:
        """Format a C4 Rel, remapping endpoints suppressed as group source shapes.

        Mermaid C4 rejects boundary ids as Rel endpoints, so a suppressed endpoint
        maps to a declared element inside that group's boundary.
        """
        endpoints = []
        for endpoint_id in (conn.from_id, conn.to_id):
            resolved: str | None = endpoint_id
            if endpoint_id not in declared_ids:
                group_id = source_to_group.get(endpoint_id)
                resolved = group_representatives.get(group_id) if group_id else None
            if resolved is None:
                warnings.warn(f'dropping C4 Rel with unresolvable endpoint {endpoint_id!r}', stacklevel=2)
                return None
            endpoints.append(self._sanitize_id(resolved))

        label = self._escape_quoted_label(conn.label or 'uses')
        return f'    Rel({endpoints[0]}, {endpoints[1]}, "{label}")'

    def _format_c4_element(self, shape: Shape, in_boundary: bool) -> str:
        keywords = _C4_BOUNDARY_KEYWORDS if in_boundary else _C4_TOP_LEVEL_KEYWORDS
        default = 'Container' if in_boundary else 'System'
        keyword = keywords.get(shape.semantic_type or '', default)
        node_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_quoted_label(shape.label or node_id)
        indent = '        ' if in_boundary else '    '
        return f'{indent}{keyword}({node_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_sequence(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate Mermaid sequence diagram."""
        lines = ['sequenceDiagram']

        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()

        for shape in shapes:
            participant_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
            label = self._escape_label(shape.label or participant_id)
            lines.append(f'    participant {participant_id} as {label}')

        for conn in connections:
            from_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.from_id)
            to_id = self._sanitize_id(conn.to_id)

            if conn.connection_type == 'bidirectional':
                arrow = '->>'
            elif conn.style.stroke_style == 'dashed':
                arrow = '-->'
            else:
                arrow = '->>'

            label = self._escape_label(conn.label or '')
            lines.append(f'    {from_id}{arrow}{to_id}: {label}')

        return '\n'.join(lines)

    _sanitize_id = staticmethod(sanitize_alnum_id)

    def _escape_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Escape label for Mermaid flowchart node syntax."""
        escaped = label.replace('&', '&')
        escaped = escaped.replace('"', '#quot;')
        escaped = escaped.replace('<', '<')
        escaped = escaped.replace('>', '>')
        return escaped.replace('\n', '<br/>')

    def _escape_quoted_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Escape label for Mermaid quoted string contexts (C4, sequence)."""
        escaped = label.replace('\\', '\\\\')
        escaped = escaped.replace('"', '\\"')
        escaped = escaped.replace('&', '&')
        escaped = escaped.replace('<', '<')
        escaped = escaped.replace('>', '>')
        return escaped.replace('\n', '<br/>')

    def _escape_pipe_label(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Escape label for Mermaid pipe-delimited connection labels."""
        escaped = label.replace('&', '&')
        escaped = escaped.replace('|', '|')
        escaped = escaped.replace('<', '<')
        escaped = escaped.replace('>', '>')
        return escaped.replace('\n', '<br/>')

class C4PlantUMLGenerator(Generator):
    """Generate C4-PlantUML from IR."""

    def generate(self, diagram: Diagram) -> str:
        """Generate C4-PlantUML diagram from IR.

        Args:
            diagram: IR Diagram object

        Returns:
            C4-PlantUML string
        """
        lines = [
            '@startuml',
            '!include https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plantuml-stdlib/C4-PlantUML/master/C4_Component.puml',
            '',
            'LAYOUT_WITH_LEGEND()',
            '',
        ]

        # Get elements
        shapes = diagram.get_shapes()
        connections = diagram.get_connections()
        groups = diagram.get_groups()

        systems = []
        containers = []
        components = []
        databases = []
        people = []

        group_source_ids = {g.source_shape_id for g in groups}
        child_ids = {child_id for g in groups for child_id in g.children}
        for shape in shapes:
            if shape.id in child_ids or shape.id in group_source_ids:
                continue
            semantic = shape.semantic_type
            if semantic == SemanticType.SYSTEM:
                systems.append(shape)
            elif semantic == SemanticType.CONTAINER:
                containers.append(shape)
            elif semantic == SemanticType.COMPONENT:
                components.append(shape)
            elif semantic == SemanticType.DATABASE:
                databases.append(shape)
            elif semantic == SemanticType.PERSON:
                people.append(shape)
            else:
                # Default to container for unknown types
                containers.append(shape)

        # Generate people
        lines.extend(self._generate_person(person) for person in people)

        # Generate systems
        lines.extend(self._generate_system(system) for system in systems)

        # Generate containers
        lines.extend(self._generate_container(container) for container in containers)

        # Generate components
        lines.extend(self._generate_component(component) for component in components)

        # Generate databases
        lines.extend(self._generate_database(database) for database in databases)

        lines.append('')

        # Generate groups as system boundaries
        shapes_by_id = {s.id: s for s in shapes}
        groups_by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
        declared_ids = {s.id for s in shapes if s.id not in child_ids and s.id not in group_source_ids}
        for group in top_level_groups(groups):
            lines.extend(self._generate_boundary(group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, declared_ids, depth=0))

        lines.append('')

        # Generate relationships; endpoints naming a suppressed container shape
        # remap to that group's declared boundary alias
        boundary_alias_by_source = {g.source_shape_id: g.id for g in groups}
        lines.extend(self._generate_relationship(conn, boundary_alias_by_source) for conn in connections)

        lines.append('@enduml')
        return '\n'.join(lines)

    def _generate_person(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Generate C4 Person element."""
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or safe_id)
        return f'Person({safe_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_system(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Generate C4 System element."""
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or safe_id)
        return f'System({safe_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_container(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Generate C4 Container element."""
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or safe_id)
        tech = shape.metadata.get('technology', '')
        if tech:
            tech = self._escape_label(tech)
            return f'Container({safe_id}, "{label}", "{tech}")'
        return f'Container({safe_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_component(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Generate C4 Component element."""
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        label = self._escape_label(shape.label or safe_id)
        return f'Component({safe_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_database(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        """Generate C4 Database element."""
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(shape.id)
        raw_label = shape.label or safe_id
        label = self._escape_label(raw_label)
        label_lower = raw_label.lower()
        tech = ''
        if 'postgres' in label_lower:
            tech = 'PostgreSQL'
        elif 'mysql' in label_lower:
            tech = 'MySQL'
        elif 'mongodb' in label_lower or 'mongo' in label_lower:
            tech = 'MongoDB'
        elif 'redis' in label_lower:
            tech = 'Redis'

        if tech:
            return f'ComponentDb({safe_id}, "{label}", "{tech}")'
        return f'ComponentDb({safe_id}, "{label}")'

    def _generate_boundary(
        self,
        group: Group,
        shapes_by_id: dict[str, Shape],
        groups_by_id: dict[str, Group],
        declared_ids: set[str],
        depth: int,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Generate C4 System_Boundary for a group, recursing into child groups."""
        indent = '  ' * depth
        safe_id = self._sanitize_id(group.id)
        label = self._escape_label(group.label or self._sanitize_id(group.source_shape_id))
        lines = [f'{indent}System_Boundary({safe_id}, "{label}") {{']

        for child_id in group.children:
            child_group = groups_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_group:
                lines.extend(self._generate_boundary(child_group, shapes_by_id, groups_by_id, declared_ids, depth + 1))
                continue
            child_shape = shapes_by_id.get(child_id)
            if child_shape and child_shape.id not in declared_ids:
                declared_ids.add(child_shape.id)
                lines.append(f'{indent}  {self._generate_boundary_element(child_shape)}')

        lines.append(f'{indent}}}')
        return lines

    def _generate_boundary_element(self, shape: Shape) -> str:
        semantic = shape.semantic_type
        if semantic == SemanticType.COMPONENT:
            return self._generate_component(shape)
        if semantic == SemanticType.DATABASE:
            return self._generate_database(shape)
        if semantic == SemanticType.PERSON:
            return self._generate_person(shape)
        if semantic == SemanticType.SYSTEM:
            return self._generate_system(shape)
        return self._generate_container(shape)

    def _generate_relationship(self, conn: Connection, boundary_alias_by_source: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """Generate C4 Rel (relationship)."""
        from_id = self._sanitize_id(boundary_alias_by_source.get(conn.from_id, conn.from_id))
        to_id = self._sanitize_id(boundary_alias_by_source.get(conn.to_id, conn.to_id))
        label = self._escape_label(conn.label or 'uses')
        return f'Rel({from_id}, {to_id}, "{label}")'

    _sanitize_id = staticmethod(sanitize_alnum_id)
    _escape_label = staticmethod(_escape_plantuml_label)
